description: Universal rendering rules for tabletop miniature-style sculpt design visualizations optimized for image-to-3D conversion - applicable to all character types

prop_visibility_modes.description: Defines how props interact with the character silhouette based on usage context

modes.presented: Prop held/displayed away from body; fully visible base-to-tip; clear negative space except at grip
modes.carried_attached: Prop worn/slung/holstered; overlap allowed at attachment zones; attachment method must be visible; item remains readable but does NOT require full base-to-tip visibility

generic_render_rules.description: Universal rendering rules applied to all prompts
rules: SINGLE SUBJECT ONLY: exactly one character/creature in the entire image. NO other figures, NO background characters, NO companions, NO additional people or animals. Only the main subject.
FIGURE-ONLY PRESENTATION: background blank/featureless (no scenery, terrain, set dressing, environmental objects, diorama elements, bases, pedestals, plinths, stands, or ground plane).

IMAGE-TO-3D OPTIMIZATION (CRITICAL): All geometry designed for clean image-to-3D mesh reconstruction. Avoid: overlapping thin elements, extreme cloth folds, dangling straps/cords near weapons, cloth intersections with props. Require: visible air gaps between all separate elements, thickened small details, simplified edges, clear form separation.

FRAMING (HARD CONSTRAINT): full-body figure entirely visible from head to feet; no cropping at ankles, knees, hips, shoulders, elbows, wrists, or head; all limbs fully inside frame; no cinematic crop, no hero crop, no portrait crop; generous negative space around entire figure.
View: three-quarter (3/4) sculpt view (~45° turntable rotation); NOT straight-on front view. Orthographic or near-orthographic projection for accurate geometry.

Camera: orthographic or neutral perspective (NOT cinematic); centered full-body framing (head-to-feet guaranteed); camera pulled back to include entire silhouette; no close-up, no medium shot, no waist-up framing; framing priority over facial detail.
Lighting: overhead key light with clear rim separation and subtle fill for edge definition. Use rim to define depth and emphasize form separation.

Design-intent anchor (CRITICAL): conceptual sculpt design visualization intended for tabletop-scale physical reproduction; illustrative art direction, not real-world documentation or evidence; do not reference existing brands or manufactured products.

Materials: uniform matte light-to-mid grey, unpainted miniature/resin model look used to communicate form only. Monochrome only — no painted colors, no dyed regions, no texture variation; no pure black or pure white. Depth indicated ONLY by geometry, not color or texture. Even diffuse response for silhouette and plane readability; smooth surfaces with hard, crisp edges.

Rendering style (CRITICAL): HIGHLY STYLIZED ILLUSTRATION — graphic silhouettes, simplified planes, posterized value bands. Clean shapes and bold secondary forms; crisp plane breaks; hard, sharp edges. Coarse-to-medium texture scale; avoid fine microtexture, micro-noise, realistic skin pores, strand-level detail. Matte materials; no specular sparkle. Not photoreal.
Miniature readability (CRITICAL): prioritize medium-scale forms and flat/smooth planar surfaces with hard, crisp edges; avoid micro-engraving, filigree, and tiny surface noise.
Minimum feature size: avoid details smaller than ~0.5mm equivalent at tabletop scale; express detail as simple graphic cuts, chamfers, or broad grooves.

Texture: bold surface detail as graphic shapes with crisp edges and clean separation. Prefer smooth planar surfaces and hard-edged form transitions; prioritize form hierarchy: big shapes first, secondary forms next; texture scale stays coarse-to-medium (no ultra-fine noise).

No photographic artifacts: avoid lens effects (flare, bokeh), film grain, subsurface scattering, volumetric glow, chromatic aberration, and heavy depth-of-field blur. Keep illustrative clarity and graphic readability.

Fur/hair rendering (furred creatures only): bold clumps/tufts with deep grooves and clean separation between masses. NO individual hairs, NO micro-fuzz, NO flyaways, NO strand-level detail. Texture as graphic shapes, not noise.

Prop visibility modes (CRITICAL): Props follow one of two visibility modes depending on usage context. PRESENTED mode: prop held/displayed away from body; fully visible base-to-tip; clear negative space between prop and torso/limbs (except at grip/contact point). CARRIED_ATTACHED mode: prop worn, slung, holstered, or sheathed; overlap with body allowed ONLY at attachment/contact zones; attachment method (sling, holster, sheath, belt loop) must be clearly visible; prop remains readable in silhouette but does NOT require full base-to-tip visibility.

Long prop geometry (CRITICAL - 3D safe): Long props (shotguns, rifles, staffs) held at side must be angled to break the camera plane with strong foreshortening. For side-held weapons: stock at hip level, muzzle/tip angled sharply upward (35-45 degrees), with the far end clearly higher than the near end in screen space. Entire prop visible from grip to tip with visible air gap separating prop from body/clothing. NO horizontal flat-plane weapons that compress into bar shapes.

Clothing intersection prevention (CRITICAL - 3D safe): Cloth (cloaks, capes, coats, robes) must flow BEHIND or TO THE SIDE of the figure only. Cloth CANNOT intersect, wrap around, or touch: arms, held weapons, carried props, or off-hand items. Cloak edges must be thick and simplified (no thin dangling fabric). Leave clear air gaps between all cloth edges and props/limbs.

Facial sculpt override (CRITICAL — 2D→3D HARD SAFE, FLATTENED): Facial features must read as low-relief, mask-like forms with extreme shallowness in depth. Overall facial depth variation should be minimal and comparable to shallow coin relief, not sculpted anatomy. No deep cuts, cavities, sockets, trenches, hollows, grooves, or undercuts anywhere on the face. Facial forms must remain near-planar when viewed in profile. Brow ridge flattened and nearly flush with the forehead—no projection, shelf, overhang, or tension shaping. Forehead, brow, cheeks, nose, and mouth constructed as broad, flat primary planes with almost no curvature; avoid rounded transitions, use soft planar blending only. Cheeks, mouth, and jaw treated as one continuous flat facial plate—no cheek definition, nasolabial indication, or mouth corner shaping. Mouth represented as a thin surface crease or shallow line break, not an opening or cavity; interior depth nearly zero. Teeth (fangs if present) indicated only as two minimal surface protrusions barely raised from the face plane; no separation or depth. Eyes represented as shallow almond depressions or raised lids only; no eye sockets, recessed eyeballs, or orbital depth. Facial expression conveyed only by silhouette, head angle, and mouth opening shape—not by facial relief, creasing, or muscular definition. Facial detail resolution intentionally lower than the rest of the figure; the face should appear simpler and flatter than armor, cloth, or equipment to discourage over-interpretation during 3D reconstruction.

MOUTH & TEETH OVERRIDE (ABSOLUTE): Mouth is not an opening. It is a single shallow surface crease stamped into the face plane, comparable to coin relief or embossed iconography. No lip separation, no interior volume, no shadow pocket. Fangs are NOT teeth: represent only as two tiny triangular surface notches interrupting the mouth crease, engraved not extruded, with negligible projection. No individual teeth, no gums, no dental anatomy, no cavities, no mouth depth. Mouth corners blunt and planar with no curvature or dimpling. Mouth detail must be lower priority than armor seams and cloth edges.
Prop constraint (CRITICAL): do not add props unless explicitly specified. Only include items clearly named and described. Do not invent extra weapons, holsters, pouches, talismans, or implements.

Small prop readability (CRITICAL - 3D safe): Small props (compact/small prop_class: crucifixes, amulets, pouches, etc.) must be forced into silhouette separation to avoid torso merging. Small props require: thickened geometry beyond realistic scale; rotation slightly outward from body plane (10-20 degrees); offset from torso with clear negative space around entire silhouette; no contact with torso, cloak, or arms. Small props represented as simplified blocky shapes with thick edges. Gear details (bandolier shells, rosary beads, pouches) rendered as large simplified cylinders or spheres, not fine realistic detail.

Strict exclusions (CRITICAL - 3D safe): NO straps, NO slings, NO ropes, NO cords, NO chains (except integrated into solid prop geometry). NO thin dangling elements. NO overlapping thin cloth. NO extreme cloth folds or bunching. NO cinematic lighting effects. NO bases, stands, ground planes, or environmental elements.
Poses: must be readable from a single view without limb/object overlap. Held objects presented away from torso with clear negative space; avoid self-occluding silhouettes.

Value contrast (CRITICAL): depth expressed through greys. Darkest recesses as deep grey (not black); brightest planes as light grey (not pure white). Avoid flat lighting; emphasize overhead lighting for readable separation. CRITICAL: Dark values represent DEPTH ONLY (recesses, undercuts, shadows) NOT color. Surface color differences (e.g., eye pupils, dark fabric) rendered as mid-grey same as surrounding surfaces; only depth changes create value shifts.
